title.zh: 卷五十五 志第二十四: 儀衞志一
title.raw: 卷五十五 志第二十四: 儀衞志一 Volume 55 Treatises 25: Ceremonial Guards 1

translations.literal: Ceremonial Guards, Part 1
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial Guards, Part 1

sentences.zh: 遼太祖奮自朔方，太宗繼誌述事，以成其業。

translations.literal: The Liao Taizu exerted himself from the northern frontier; Taizong carried on his will and recorded his deeds, thereby completing the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu of Liao rose to power from the northern frontier, and Emperor Taizong continued his purpose and consolidated his achievements, bringing the enterprise to completion.

sentences.zh: 於是舉渤海，立敬瑭，破重貴，盡致周、秦、兩漢、隋、唐文物之遺餘而居有之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he raised up Bohai, enthroned Jingtang, defeated Chonggui, and fully gathered the surviving cultural relics of Zhou, Qin, the two Han dynasties, Sui, and Tang and took possession of them.
translations.idiomatic: He then subjugated Bohai, installed Shi Jingtang, defeated Shi Chonggui, and gathered into his possession the surviving regalia and artifacts of Zhou, Qin, both Han dynasties, Sui, and Tang.

sentences.zh: 路車法物以隆等威，金符玉璽以布號令。

translations.literal: State chariots and ritual objects to elevate rank and majesty; gold tallies and jade seals to issue commands.
translations.idiomatic: He employed state chariots and ritual regalia to enhance hierarchical grandeur, and gold tallies and jade seals to promulgate his commands.

sentences.zh: 是以傳至九主二百餘年，豈獨以兵革之利，士馬之強哉！

translations.literal: Thus the succession passed through nine rulers for more than two hundred years—was it solely by the advantage of arms and the strength of men and horses!
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty endured through nine rulers over more than two centuries—surely this was not due to military advantage and cavalry strength alone!

sentences.zh: 文謂之儀，武謂之衛，足以成一代之規模矣。

translations.literal: What is civil is called ceremony; what is martial is called guard—sufficient to form the model of an age.
translations.idiomatic: Civil affairs were called ceremonial protocol and military affairs ceremonial guard—together they sufficed to establish the institutional framework of an entire dynasty.

sentences.zh: 考遼所有輿服、符璽、儀仗，作《儀衛志》。

translations.literal: Examining all chariots, attire, tallies, seals, and ceremonial regalia of the Liao, I compose the "Treatise on Ceremonial Guards."
translations.idiomatic: Surveying the Liao's chariots and attire, seals and tallies, and ceremonial regalia, I have compiled the Treatise on Ceremonial Guards.

translations.literal: ○ Chariots and Attire
translations.idiomatic: Chariots and Attire

sentences.zh: 自黃帝而降，輿服之制，其來遠矣。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor downward, the institutions of chariots and attire have come from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Since the time of the Yellow Emperor, the institutions governing chariots and ceremonial dress reach far back into antiquity.

sentences.zh: 禹乘四載作小車，商人得桑根之瑞為大輅，周人加金玉，象飾益備。

translations.literal: Yu rode the four conveyances and made small carts; the Shang obtained the auspice of mulberry root and made the great chariot; the Zhou added gold and jade, and elephant ornamentation grew ever more complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yu employed the four transport modes and devised small carts; the Shang, receiving the auspicious sign of mulberry root, fashioned the great state chariot; the Zhou added gold and jade until elephant ornamentation was fully arrayed.

sentences.zh: 秦取六國儀物，而分別其用，先王之制，置而弗禦。

translations.literal: Qin took the ritual objects of the six states and distinguished their uses; the institutions of former kings were set aside and not employed.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin seized the ritual paraphernalia of the six states and assigned separate uses to each, while the institutions of earlier kings were set aside and no longer employed.

sentences.zh: 至漢中葉，銳意稽古，然禮文之事，名存實亡，蓋得十一於千百焉。

translations.literal: By the mid-Han, they keenly investigated antiquity, yet in ritual matters the name survived while the substance perished—perhaps one part in a thousand remained.
translations.idiomatic: By the middle Han, antiquarian restoration was pursued with vigor, yet in ritual matters names survived while substance vanished—perhaps no more than one part in a thousand remained intact.

sentences.zh: 唐之車輅因周、隋遺法，損益可知。

translations.literal: The Tang chariots followed the legacy methods of Zhou and Sui; additions and subtractions can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Tang ceremonial chariots followed the inherited methods of Zhou and Sui, and their modifications can be traced.

sentences.zh: 而祭服皆青，朝服皆絳，常服用宇文制，以紫、緋、綠、碧分品秩。

translations.literal: Sacrificial robes were all green; court robes all crimson; ordinary dress followed Yuwen's system, using purple, scarlet, green, and blue-green to distinguish ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial robes were uniformly green, court robes crimson, and ordinary dress followed the Yuwen system, with purple, scarlet, green, and blue-green distinguishing ranks.

translations.literal: The Five Dynasties largely used ordinary dress in place of court robes.
translations.idiomatic: During the Five Dynasties, ordinary dress largely replaced formal court attire.

sentences.zh: 遼國自太宗入晉之後，皇帝與南班漢官用漢服；

translations.literal: From the time the Liao entered Jin after Taizong, the emperor and Han officials of the southern bureau used Han dress;
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taizong's entry into the Jin capital, the emperor and Han officials of the southern court wore Chinese-style dress;

sentences.zh: 太后與北班契丹臣僚用國服，其漢服即五代晉之遺制也。

translations.literal: the empress dowager and Khitan officials of the northern bureau used national dress; the Han dress was precisely the surviving institution of Jin in the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: while the empress dowager and Khitan officials of the northern court wore Khitan national dress. The Chinese dress was the legacy of Later Jin during the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 考之載籍之可徵者，著《輿服篇》，冠諸《儀衛》之首。

translations.literal: Examining what can be verified in written records, I set forth the "Section on Chariots and Attire," placing it at the head of "Ceremonial Guards."
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on verifiable entries in the historical record, I present the section on chariots and attire as the opening chapter of the Treatise on Ceremonial Guards.

translations.literal: The old Khitan custom favored saddles and horses.
translations.idiomatic: By ancient Khitan custom, saddle and horse were the norm.

sentences.zh: 隨水草遷徙，則有氈車，任載有大車，婦人乘馬，亦有小車，貴富者加之華飾。

translations.literal: Following water and pasture in migration, there were felt carts; for heavy loads there were large carts; women rode horses, and there were also small carts; the wealthy added splendid ornament.
translations.idiomatic: When moving with the seasons after pasture and water, they used felt carts; heavy loads went on large wagons; women rode horseback, and small carts were also used—the wealthy adding lavish ornament.

translations.literal: Prohibitions were lax; what was valued was practical use alone.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were loose, and utility alone was prized.

translations.literal: For emperors and empresses additional grandeur was added—the momentum was naturally so.
translations.idiomatic: For emperors and empresses, further grandeur was added—a natural consequence of their station.

translations.literal: I gather what can be known and set it down in this section.
translations.idiomatic: What can be established is compiled in the account that follows.

sentences.zh: 大輿，《柴冊再生儀》載神主見之。

translations.literal: Great carriage: in the "Rite of the Spirit Tablet's Rebirth from the Timber Register" the spirit tablet is conveyed upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Great carriage—in the Rite of the Spirit Tablet's Rebirth from the Timber Register, the spirit tablet is borne upon it.

sentences.zh: 輿，《臘儀》見皇帝、皇后升輿、降輿。

translations.literal: Palanquin: in the "Lunar New Year Rite" the emperor and empress are seen ascending and descending the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Palanquin—in the Lunar New Year Rite, the emperor and empress are shown mounting and dismounting it.

translations.literal: Great-banner cart, drawn by imperial camels.
translations.idiomatic: Great-banner cart—drawn by imperial camels.

translations.literal: In the "Mountain Sacrifice Rite" the empress dowager is seen ascending the great-banner cart.
translations.idiomatic: In the Mountain Sacrifice Rite, the empress dowager ascends the great-banner cart.

translations.literal: Cart: in the "Rite of Receiving the Empress" the empress is seen entering the cart.
translations.idiomatic: Cart—in the Rite of Receiving the Empress, the empress enters the cart.

sentences.zh: 青幰車，二螭頭、蓋部皆飾以銀。

translations.literal: Green-canopied cart: both dragon heads and the canopy frame are ornamented with silver.
translations.idiomatic: Green-canopied cart—both dragon-head fittings and the canopy frame are decorated in silver.

sentences.zh: 駕用駝，公主下嫁以賜之。

translations.literal: Drawn by camels; bestowed when a princess marries out.
translations.idiomatic: It is drawn by camels and is bestowed when a princess marries out of the royal house.

sentences.zh: 古者王姬下嫁，車服不系其夫，下王後一等。

translations.literal: In antiquity when a king's daughter married out, chariot and dress were not tied to her husband's rank but were one grade below the queen's.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when a king's daughter married abroad, her chariot and regalia were not bound to her husband's rank but set one grade below that of the queen.

translations.literal: Is this perhaps the surviving intent?
translations.idiomatic: Does this perhaps preserve that ancient intent?

sentences.zh: 送終車，車樓純飾以錦，螭頭以銀，下縣鐸，後垂大氈，駕以牛。

translations.literal: Funeral-conveyance cart: the cart frame is adorned entirely in brocade; dragon heads in silver; bells suspended below; a great felt hanging behind; drawn by oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral-conveyance cart—the carriage superstructure is draped entirely in brocade, dragon-head fittings in silver, bells hung beneath, a large felt curtain trailing behind, and oxen as the draft animals.

sentences.zh: 上載羊一，謂之祭羊，以擬送終之用。

translations.literal: Upon it is loaded one sheep, called the sacrificial sheep, to simulate funeral use.
translations.idiomatic: A sheep is loaded aboard, called the sacrificial sheep, to stand for the funeral offering.

translations.literal: It is also bestowed on princesses.
translations.idiomatic: This cart is also bestowed upon princesses.

sentences.zh: 椅，《冊皇太后儀》，皇帝乘椅，自便殿瑽至西便門。

translations.literal: Sedan chair: in the "Rite of Enthroning the Empress Dowager," the emperor rides the chair from the side hall Zong to the Western Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sedan chair—in the Rite of Enthroning the Empress Dowager, the emperor is carried in a sedan chair from the Side Hall of Jasper to the Western Convenient Gate.

sentences.zh: 鞍馬，《祭山儀》，皇帝乘馬，侍皇太后行。

translations.literal: Saddle horse: in the "Mountain Sacrifice Rite," the emperor rides a horse and attends the empress dowager in procession.
translations.idiomatic: Saddle horse—in the Mountain Sacrifice Rite, the emperor rides horseback and attends the empress dowager in procession.

sentences.zh: 《臘儀》，皇帝降輿，祭東畢，乘馬入豬圍。

translations.literal: In the "Lunar New Year Rite," the emperor descends from the palanquin, the eastern sacrifice completed, rides a horse into the pig enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: In the Lunar New Year Rite, the emperor dismounts from his palanquin after completing the eastern sacrifice and rides into the pig enclosure.

sentences.zh: 《瑟瑟儀》，俱乘馬東行，群臣在南，命婦在北。

translations.literal: In the "Sese Rite," all ride horses eastward; ministers are on the south, titled women on the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sese Rite, all ride eastward on horseback—ministers to the south, titled ladies to the north.

translations.literal: Han Chariots
translations.idiomatic: Han Chariots

translations.literal: Five chariots: the "Rites of Zhou" Court of Chariots lists five chariots.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Chariots—the Director of Chariots in the Rites of Zhou maintains five ritual chariots.

translations.literal: After the fall of Qin, Han created its own institutions.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qin fell, the Han established its own system.

sentences.zh: 玉輅，祀天、祭地、享宗廟、朝賀、納後用之。

translations.literal: Jade chariot: used for sacrificing to Heaven, sacrificing to Earth, offering in the ancestral temple, court congratulations, and receiving the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Jade chariot—used for sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, offerings in the ancestral temple, court audiences of congratulation, and receiving the empress.

translations.literal: Green material, jade ornament, yellow canopy, great banner on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Green body, jade fittings, yellow canopy, and the great banner mounted on the left.

translations.literal: Twelve pennons on the crossbar, two bells on the chariot rail.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve pennon pendants on the crossbar and two bells on the handrail.

sentences.zh: 龍辀左建旂，十二遊，皆畫升龍，長曳地。

translations.literal: On the dragon-shaft carriage pole a banner is erected on the left; twelve tassels, all painted with ascending dragons, trail long to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: On the left of the dragon-shaft pole a banner is raised; twelve streamers, each painted with ascending dragons, trail to the ground.

sentences.zh: 駕蒼龍，金摐，鏤錫，鞶纓十二就。

translations.literal: Drawn by blue-green horses, golden bustle, carved tin, twelve sets of braided caparison.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by grey-green horses with golden fittings, carved tin ornaments, and twelve sets of braided trappings.

sentences.zh: 遼國《勘箭儀》，皇帝乘玉輅至內門。

translations.literal: In the Liao "Arrow-Verification Rite," the emperor rides the jade chariot to the inner gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liao Arrow-Verification Rite, the emperor rides the jade chariot to the inner gate.

sentences.zh: 聖宗開泰十年，上升玉輅自內三門入萬壽殿，進七廟御容酒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Emperor Shengzong's Kaitai era, ascending the jade chariot he entered the Hall of Ten Thousand Longevities from the inner triple gates and presented wine before the imperial portraits of the seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaitai 10 of Emperor Shengzong's reign, he mounted the jade chariot, entered the Hall of Ten Thousand Longevities through the inner triple gates, and presented wine before the imperial portraits in the seven ancestral shrines.

sentences.zh: 金輅，饗射、祀還、飲至用之。

translations.literal: Gold chariot: used for archery feasts, return from sacrifice, and victory banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Gold chariot—used for archery feasts, the return from sacrifice, and victory banquets.

sentences.zh: 赤質，金飾，余如玉輅，色從其質。

translations.literal: Red material, gold ornament; the rest like the jade chariot; color follows its material.
translations.idiomatic: Red body and gold fittings; otherwise like the jade chariot, with color matching the material.

translations.literal: Drawn by chestnut horses.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by chestnut horses.

translations.literal: Ivory chariot: used for traveling on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Ivory chariot—used when traveling on official journeys.

translations.literal: Yellow material, ivory ornament; the rest like the gold chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow body with ivory fittings; otherwise like the gold chariot.

translations.literal: Drawn by yellow horses.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by yellow horses.

translations.literal: Leather chariot: used for imperial tours and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Leather chariot—used for imperial inspection tours and military affairs.

translations.literal: White material, leather-covered.
translations.idiomatic: White body with leather covering.

translations.literal: Drawn by white Han horses.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by white Han horses.

translations.literal: Wooden chariot: used for hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Wooden chariot—used for the royal hunt.

translations.literal: Black material, lacquer ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Black body with lacquer ornament.

translations.literal: Drawn by black camels.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by black camels.

translations.literal: Cart: smaller in form than the chariots; used for minor affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cart—of smaller build than the ritual chariots, used for lesser occasions.

translations.literal: Plough-root cart: used for the ploughing and harvesting ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Plough-root cart—used in the ceremonial ploughing and first-fruits rite.

translations.literal: Green material, triple canopy; the rest like the jade chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Green body with triple canopy; otherwise like the jade chariot.

sentences.zh: 安車，一名進賢車，臨幸用之。

translations.literal: Peace chariot, also called the Promoting the Worthy chariot; used for imperial visits.
translations.idiomatic: Sedan chariot, also called the Promoting the Worthy chariot—used when the emperor pays a personal visit.

sentences.zh: 金飾重輿，曲壁，八鑾在衡，紫油纁，朱裏幰，朱絲絡網。

translations.literal: Gold-ornamented with heavy carriage frame, curved walls, eight pennons on the crossbar, purple oil on reddish cloth, vermilion inner canopy, vermilion silk net.
translations.idiomatic: Heavily built with gold ornament, curved side panels, eight pennons on the crossbar, purple oil finish on reddish cloth, vermilion inner canopy lining, and a vermilion silk mesh net.

translations.literal: Drawn by chestnut horses with vermilion braided caparison.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by chestnut horses with vermilion braided trappings.

sentences.zh: 四望車，一名明遠車，拜陵、臨吊則用之。

translations.literal: Four-View chariot, also called the Bright-Distance chariot; used for visiting tombs and offering condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Four-View chariot, also called the Bright-Distance chariot—used when paying respects at imperial tombs or offering condolences.

translations.literal: Gold ornament, blue oil on reddish cloth, vermilion inner lining, full canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Gold fittings, blue oil on reddish cloth, vermilion inner lining, and a fully enclosed canopy.

translations.literal: Drawn by oxen; the rest the same as the peace chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by oxen; otherwise the same as the sedan chariot.

sentences.zh: 涼車，赤質，省方、罷獵用之。

translations.literal: Cool chariot, red material; used for touring the provinces and ending the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Cool chariot with red body—used when the emperor tours the provinces or concludes a hunt.

translations.literal: Red material, gold plated, silver fitted.
translations.idiomatic: Red body with gold plating and silver fittings.

sentences.zh: 五彩龍風織，藤油壁，緋絳，蓮座。

translations.literal: Five-colored dragon-and-phoenix brocade, rattan oil walls, scarlet reddish trim, lotus seat.
translations.idiomatic: Five-colored dragon-and-phoenix brocade, rattan oil-finished walls, scarlet trim, and a lotus seat.

translations.literal: Drawn by Bactrian camels.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by Bactrian camels.

translations.literal: Palanquin: drawn by men; originally used within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Palanquin—man-drawn; originally used for travel within the palace.

translations.literal: Tang Gaozong first instituted seven palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong of Tang first established the seven palanquins.

translations.literal: The "Rites of Zhou" Chief Carriage Officer has palanquins, drawn by men in teams.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou assigns palanquins to the Chief Carriage Officer, drawn by teams of men.

translations.literal: In the Taiping enthronement rite, the emperor mounts the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiping Enthronement Rite, the emperor takes the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 大鳳輦，赤質，頂有金鳳，壁畫雲氣金翅。

translations.literal: Great Phoenix palanquin: red material, a golden phoenix atop, walls painted with cloud motifs and golden wings.
translations.idiomatic: Great Phoenix palanquin—red body, golden phoenix on the crown, walls painted with clouds and golden wings.

translations.literal: A rail at the front, a balustrade below.
translations.idiomatic: A front rail and a balustrade at the base.

translations.literal: Trailing straps all embroidered with cloud-phoenix motifs; silver steps.
translations.idiomatic: Trailing straps embroidered with clouds and phoenixes; silver steps.

translations.literal: Eighty men to draw the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty bearers draw the palanquin.

translations.literal: Great Fragrant palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Great Fragrant palanquin.

translations.literal: Immortal Roaming palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Immortal Roaming palanquin.

sentences.zh: 小輦，《永壽節儀》，皇太后乘小輦。

translations.literal: Small palanquin: in the "Eternal Longevity Festival Rite," the empress dowager rides the small palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Small palanquin—in the Eternal Longevity Festival Rite, the empress dowager rides the small palanquin.

sentences.zh: 芳亭輦，黑質，幕屋緋欄，皆繡雲鳳。

translations.literal: Fragrant Pavilion palanquin: black material, canopy house with scarlet rails, all embroidered with cloud-phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Fragrant Pavilion palanquin—black body, canopy pavilion with scarlet rails, all embroidered with clouds and phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 朱綠夾窗，花板紅網，兩簾四竿，銀飾梯。

translations.literal: Vermilion and green flanking windows, flower panels with red net, two curtains and four poles, silver-ornamented steps.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion-and-green flanking windows, floral panels with red mesh, two curtains on four poles, and silver-fitted steps.

translations.literal: One hundred twenty men to draw the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred twenty bearers draw the palanquin.

translations.literal: Great Jade palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jade palanquin.

translations.literal: Small Jade palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Small Jade palanquin.

translations.literal: Leisure palanquin: used for ordinary travel.
translations.idiomatic: Leisure-roaming palanquin—used for everyday travel.

sentences.zh: 棕屋，赤質，金塗，銀裝，紅絳。

translations.literal: Palm-wood house, red material, gold plated, silver fitted, red trim.
translations.idiomatic: Palm-frond canopy, red body, gold plating, silver fittings, and red trim.

sentences.zh: 輦官十二人，春夏緋衫，秋冬素錦服。

translations.literal: Twelve palanquin officers; scarlet jackets in spring and summer, plain brocade robes in autumn and winter.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve palanquin attendants wear scarlet jackets in spring and summer and plain brocade robes in autumn and winter.

translations.literal: Flat-Top palanquin: used for ordinary travel.
translations.idiomatic: Flat-Top palanquin—used for everyday travel.

translations.literal: The form like the Leisure palanquin but without a canopy house.
translations.idiomatic: Of the same design as the Leisure palanquin but without a canopy structure.

sentences.zh: 冊承天皇太后儀，皇太后乘平頭輦。

translations.literal: In the rite of enthroning the Empress Dowager Who Received Heaven, the empress dowager rides the Flat-Top palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rite of Enthroning the Empress Dowager Who Received Heaven, the empress dowager rides the Flat-Top palanquin.

sentences.zh: 步輦，聖宗統和三年，駐蹕土河，乘步輦聽政。

translations.literal: Hand palanquin: in the third year of Emperor Shengzong's Tonghe era, encamped at the Tuh River, he rode the hand palanquin to attend to government.
translations.idiomatic: Hand-borne palanquin—in Tonghe 3 of Emperor Shengzong's reign, while encamped at the Tuh River, he conducted state business from a hand palanquin.

translations.literal: Sheep cart: an ancient palanquin cart.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep cart—an ancient type of palanquin carriage.

sentences.zh: 赤質，兩壁龜文、鳳翅，緋幰，絡帶、門簾皆繡瑞羊，畫輪。

translations.literal: Red material; both walls with tortoise patterns and phoenix wings; scarlet canopy; trailing straps and door curtains all embroidered with auspicious sheep; painted wheels.
translations.idiomatic: Red body; tortoise patterns and phoenix wings on both walls; scarlet canopy; trailing straps and door curtains embroidered with auspicious sheep; painted wheels.

translations.literal: Originally drawn by oxen; in Sui changed to pony horses.
translations.idiomatic: Originally drawn by oxen; the Sui replaced these with pony horses.

sentences.zh: 童子十八人，服繡，瑞羊免之。

translations.literal: Eighteen youths in embroidered dress, with caps fashioned as auspicious sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen attendants in embroidered robes wear caps fashioned like auspicious sheep.

sentences.zh: 輿：以人肩之，天子用韝絡臂綰。

translations.literal: Palanquin: borne on men's shoulders; the Son of Heaven uses leather shoulder-straps with braided cords tied at the arm.
translations.idiomatic: Palanquin—borne on bearers' shoulders; the emperor uses leather shoulder-straps with braided arm ties.

sentences.zh: 腰輿，前後長竿各二，金銀螭頭，緋繡鳳襕，上施錦褥，別設小床。

translations.literal: Waist palanquin: front and rear two long poles each, gold and silver dragon heads, scarlet embroidered phoenix panels, a brocade mat above, with a separate small couch.
translations.idiomatic: Waist palanquin—two long poles fore and aft, gold and silver dragon-head fittings, scarlet-embroidered phoenix panels, a brocade mat above, and a separate small couch.

translations.literal: Sixteen men to bear the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen bearers carry the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 小輿，赤質，青頂，曲柄，緋繡絡帶。

translations.literal: Small palanquin: red material, green peak, curved handles, scarlet embroidered trailing straps.
translations.idiomatic: Small palanquin—red body, green crown, curved handles, and scarlet-embroidered trailing straps.

sentences.zh: 制如鳳輦而小，上有御座。

translations.literal: The form like the Phoenix palanquin but smaller, with an imperial seat above.
translations.idiomatic: Of the same design as the Phoenix palanquin but smaller, with an imperial seat mounted above.

translations.literal: Twenty-four men to bear the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four bearers carry the palanquin.

translations.literal: Crown Prince's chariots:
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's Chariots:

sentences.zh: 金輅，從祀享、正冬大朝、納妃用之。

translations.literal: Gold chariot: used for accompanying sacrificial offerings, the great winter court audience, and receiving a consort.
translations.idiomatic: Gold chariot—used when accompanying sacrificial offerings, at the great winter court audience, and when receiving a consort.

sentences.zh: 《冊皇太子儀》，乘黃令陳金輅，皇太子升、降金輅。

translations.literal: In the "Rite of Enthroning the Crown Prince," the Bearer-of-Yellow presents the gold chariot; the crown prince ascends and descends the gold chariot.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rite of Enthroning the Crown Prince, the Bearer-of-the Yellow presents the gold chariot, and the crown prince mounts and dismounts it.

sentences.zh: 軺車，五日常朝、享宮臣、出入行道用之。

translations.literal: Light cart: used for the fifth-day regular court, feasting palace ministers, and going out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Light carriage—used for the fifth-day regular audience, entertaining palace ministers, and everyday travel on official business.

translations.literal: Gold ornament, purple canopy with vermilion inner lining.
translations.idiomatic: Gold fittings with a purple canopy and vermilion inner lining.

translations.literal: Drawn by one horse.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by a single horse.

translations.literal: Four-View chariot: used for offering condolence on mourning visits.
translations.idiomatic: Four-View chariot—used when paying condolence visits.

translations.literal: Gold ornament, purple oil on reddish cloth, full canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Gold fittings with purple oil on reddish cloth and a fully enclosed canopy.

translations.literal: Drawn by one horse.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn by a single horse.
